questions.question: As of July 2025, how many Indian States have a bicameral legislature (i.e. both, a Legislative Assembly and a Legislative Council)?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Six**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India has a **federal parliamentary system** and legislative bodies at both the central and state levels.
 
• A bicameral legislature consists of two houses: the **Legislative Assembly (Vidhan Sabha)** and the **Legislative Council (Vidhan Parishad).**
 
• As of **July 2025**, there are **six Indian states** with a bicameral legislature. These states are **Uttar Pradesh, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Bihar, Andhra Pradesh, and Telangana.**
 
• The **Legislative Council** is a permanent body and cannot be dissolved, but members retire in rotation.
 
• The creation or abolition of a Legislative Council is governed by **Article 169** of the Indian Constitution. A state legislature can pass a resolution by a special majority to create or abolish a council.
 
• The **Legislative Assembly**, on the other hand, is directly elected by the people of the state and has significant powers, including passing state laws, budget approvals, and discussions on government policies.
 
• Bicameral legislatures are intended to ensure better representation of diverse interests and to provide a mechanism for deeper scrutiny of legislation.
 
• The states with bicameral legislatures represent a mix of **large populations, economic significance, and historical contexts** that justify the presence of two houses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eight States**__

 __
 
• India has only **six states** with bicameral legislatures, not eight. This option is incorrect as it suggests a higher number than the actual count.
 
 
 
• **Seven States**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect as India has **six states** with bicameral legislatures, not seven.
 
 
 
• **Five States**__
 
 
• While some states have unicameral legislatures, the number of states with bicameral legislatures in India is **six**, making this option incorrect.

questions.question: In Indian State governments, to whom is the State Council of Ministers collectively responsible?

options.text: Chief Justice of the concerned State

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**State Legislative Assembly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Council of Ministers** in India is collectively responsible to the **State Legislative Assembly**, as per Article 164 of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The **State Legislative Assembly**, also called the **Vidhan Sabha**, is the lower house of the state legislature in states with a bicameral legislature or the sole legislative body in states with a unicameral legislature.
 
• This principle of collective responsibility ensures that the council acts as a single entity and is accountable to the legislature for its policies and decisions.
 
• If the Legislative Assembly passes a vote of no confidence against the Council of Ministers, they are bound to resign collectively, including the Chief Minister.
 
• The **Chief Minister**, as the head of the Council of Ministers, plays a key role in ensuring the accountability of the council to the Legislative Assembly.
 
• This system is a fundamental aspect of the **parliamentary system of government** in India and is modeled on the British parliamentary system.
 
• The Legislative Assembly comprises elected representatives of the people, making it the most appropriate body for ensuring the accountability of the executive branch to the citizens.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Governor of the State**__

 __
 
• The **Governor** is the constitutional head of the state and acts on the advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister.
 
• While the Governor appoints the Chief Minister and other ministers, the Council of Ministers is not collectively responsible to the Governor.
 
• The Governor has certain discretionary powers, but the executive powers of the state are exercised by the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• **Council of States**__
 __
 
• The **Council of States**, commonly referred to as the **Rajya Sabha**, is the upper house of the Indian Parliament and does not play a direct role in the functioning of state governments.
 
• It represents the interests of the states at the national level and primarily deals with matters concerning the Union and its territories.
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of the concerned State**__
 
 
• The **Chief Justice of the High Court** is the head of the judiciary in a state and ensures justice under the legal framework.
 
• The judiciary functions independently of the executive and legislature and does not have a role in the accountability of the Council of Ministers.

questions.question: Although a colloid appears homogeneous, it is actually a __________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**heterogeneous mixture**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Although a colloid appears to be **homogeneous**, it is actually a **heterogeneous mixture**.
 
• A colloid consists of two phases: the **dispersed phase** (particles) and the **dispersing medium** (continuous phase).
 
• The particles in a colloid are **microscopic** and do not settle at the bottom over time, making it look uniform.
 
• Colloids exhibit the **Tyndall effect**, where light is scattered due to the dispersed particles.
 
• The size of colloidal particles typically ranges between **1 nanometer and 100 nanometers**, distinguishing it from other mixtures.
 
• Examples of colloids include **milk, fog, and jelly**.
 
• This heterogeneous nature is critical for the unique properties of colloids, such as their stability and ability to scatter light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Suspension**__

 __
 
• A **suspension** is a heterogeneous mixture where the particles are large enough to settle out over time.
 
• Examples include **sand in water** or **muddy water**.
 
• Suspensions do not exhibit the **Tyndall effect** as the particles are too large to scatter light effectively.
 
 
 
• **True solution**__
 __
 
• A **true solution** is a homogeneous mixture where the solute is completely dissolved in the solvent.
 
• Examples include **sugar in water** or **salt in water**.
 
• True solutions do not exhibit the **Tyndall effect** as the particles are molecular in size.
 
 
 
• **Homogeneous mixture**__
 
 
• A **homogeneous mixture** has a uniform composition throughout, such as **air** or **vinegar**.
 
• It does not have any dispersed particles or phases, making it different from a colloid.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures do not scatter light and are transparent when in liquid form.

questions.question: What happens when you delete a file or folder using the Delete key?

options.text: The file is copied to another folder.
The file is sent to the Recycle Bin.
The file is permanently deleted without warning.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The file is sent to the Recycle Bin.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When you delete a file or folder using the **Delete key** on a Windows computer, the file is not permanently deleted. Instead, it is sent to the **Recycle Bin.**
 
• The **Recycle Bin** serves as a temporary storage location for deleted files, allowing users to restore files that may have been deleted accidentally.
 
• Files remain in the **Recycle Bin** until the user manually empties it or it reaches its storage limit, after which the oldest files are removed automatically.
 
• This feature acts as a safeguard against accidental deletion and ensures that users have the ability to recover important files if needed.
 
• To permanently delete a file without moving it to the Recycle Bin, users can use the **Shift + Delete** keyboard shortcut.
 
• The **Recycle Bin** is typically accessible from the desktop, and users can review and restore files by right-clicking on them and selecting the **Restore** option.
 
• The functionality of the **Recycle Bin** is a built-in feature of Windows operating systems and is widely used to manage deleted files efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The file is copied to another folder.**__

 __
 
• This option is incorrect because deleting a file does not copy it to another folder.
 
• Copying a file requires a separate action, such as using the **Ctrl + C** and **Ctrl + V** keyboard shortcuts or the context menu options.
 
 
 
• **The file is renamed automatically.**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because deleting a file does not rename it automatically.
 
• Renaming a file requires the user to manually select the file, right-click on it, and choose the **Rename** option or use the **F2 key**.
 
 
 
• **The file is permanently deleted without warning.**__
 
 
• This option is incorrect because files deleted using the **Delete key** are not permanently removed.
 
• Permanently deleting files typically involves using the **Shift + Delete** keyboard combination, bypassing the **Recycle Bin**.

• Both Nepal and Bhutan share **only land borders** with India and do not have any coastline or maritime boundary.
 
• **Nepal** is bordered by India on three sides (east, south, and west) and by **China** in the north.
 
• **Bhutan** shares its borders with India in the south, east, and west, while it is bordered by **China** in the north.

• Both countries are surrounded by water and are not landlocked.

questions.question: Which postulate of Dalton’s atomic theory reflects the Law of Conservation of Mass?

options.text: Atoms cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.
Atoms of different elements have different masses and properties.
Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds.
All matter is made up of indivisible particles called atoms.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Atoms cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The statement "**Atoms cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction**" aligns directly with the **Law of Conservation of Mass**, which states that **mass in a closed system remains constant** during a chemical reaction.
 
• Dalton's atomic theory postulated that **atoms are indestructible and unchangeable**. This principle ensures that the total mass of reactants and products in a chemical reaction remains equal.
 
• The **Law of Conservation of Mass** was formulated by **Antoine Lavoisier**, who demonstrated that matter cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed.
 
• This concept is fundamental in chemical equations, where the **number of atoms** of each element must be balanced on both sides of the reaction.
 
• Dalton's idea strengthened the understanding of **chemical processes**, emphasizing that no atom vanishes or appears during reactions, ensuring the conservation of matter.
 
• This principle forms the basis of stoichiometry, which deals with the calculation of reactants and products in chemical reactions.
 
• It is particularly significant in industries such as **pharmaceuticals, petrochemicals, and material science**, where precise chemical reactions are crucial.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Atoms of different elements have different masses and properties.**__

 __
 
• This postulate highlights the **unique identity of each element**, as the atoms of one element differ in **mass, size, and chemical properties** from atoms of other elements.
 
• It explains why different elements exhibit distinct behaviors, forming compounds with specific properties.
 
• This principle is crucial in understanding the **Periodic Table**, where elements are arranged based on their atomic properties.
 
 
 
• **Atoms combine in simple whole-number ratios to form compounds.**__
 __
 
• This postulate is related to the **Law of Definite Proportions**, which states that chemical compounds are composed of elements in fixed ratios by mass.
 
• For example, water (H₂O) always consists of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
 
• It forms the foundation for understanding **chemical bonding** and molecular structures.
 
 
 
• **All matter is made up of indivisible particles called atoms.**__
 
 
• This postulate introduced the idea that **atoms are the basic building blocks of matter**.
 
• Though later developments in science showed that atoms can be divided into subatomic particles, the concept remains fundamental to understanding matter's structure.
 
• It is crucial in the fields of **physics, chemistry, and material science** for studying the properties and behavior of matter.

questions.question: The 'Montreal Protocol' was signed to control the emission of _____.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**chlorofluorocarbons**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Montreal Protocol** was adopted in **1987** and is an international treaty designed to protect the **ozone layer**.
 
• Its primary goal is to phase out the production and consumption of **ozone-depleting substances (ODS)**, particularly **chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)**.
 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs)** are compounds containing **carbon, chlorine, and fluorine**, and they are commonly used in refrigeration, air conditioning, and aerosol sprays.
 
• CFCs release **chlorine atoms** into the atmosphere, which react with ozone molecules, leading to the **depletion of the ozone layer**.
 
• The depletion of the ozone layer causes harmful **ultraviolet (UV) radiation** to reach the Earth's surface, leading to various health and environmental issues such as **skin cancer**, cataracts, and damage to ecosystems.
 
• The **Montreal Protocol** is considered one of the most successful international environmental agreements, as it has significantly reduced the use of CFCs globally.
 
• The treaty has been ratified by almost all countries and has led to the recovery of the ozone layer, which is expected to return to its pre-1980 levels by the middle of the **21st century**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Carbon dioxide**__

 __
 
• **Carbon dioxide (CO₂)** is a greenhouse gas that contributes to **global warming** and climate change.
 
• It is primarily emitted through the burning of **fossil fuels**, deforestation, and industrial processes.
 
• Although CO₂ is not directly responsible for ozone depletion, its increasing concentration in the atmosphere is linked to adverse climate effects.
 
 
 
• **Methane**__
 __
 
• **Methane (CH₄)** is another potent greenhouse gas that contributes to **global warming**.
 
• It is released through activities such as **agriculture** (e.g., livestock farming), the decay of organic matter, and the extraction of **natural gas**.
 
• While methane does not deplete the ozone layer, it has a significant impact on climate change.
 
 
 
• **Sulphur dioxide**__
 
 
• **Sulphur dioxide (SO₂)** is primarily produced through the burning of **coal and oil**, as well as volcanic eruptions.
 
• SO₂ contributes to the formation of **acid rain**, which can damage ecosystems, buildings, and human health.
 
• Unlike CFCs, SO₂ does not play a direct role in ozone depletion but has environmental impacts in other ways.

questions.question: What key principle did the Supreme Court emphasise in the 2024 Property Owners Association v State of Maharashtra case?

options.text: Only scarce or vital resources justify state takeover
Public trust doctrine applies to all private assets.
State can acquire all private properties at will.
Government power overrides individual property rights.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only scarce or vital resources justify state takeover**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Supreme Court highlighted that the principle of state takeover applies only to **resources that are scarce or vital** for public interest.
 
• This decision reinforces the idea that state intervention in private property must be **well-justified** and limited to cases where it is necessary for **public welfare**.
 
• The judgment is significant as it places a **limit on the state's authority** over private property, safeguarding **individual rights**.
 
• It aligns with the constitutional provisions in India, particularly **Article 300A**, which ensures that private property can only be acquired under the authority of law.
 
• By emphasizing this principle, the Supreme Court aims to prevent misuse of power and protect the rights of **property owners**.
 
• It also reflects the judiciary's commitment to upholding the **rule of law** in cases related to property rights and acquisition.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Public trust doctrine applies to all private assets**__

 __
 
• This doctrine suggests that certain resources are preserved for public use and the government must protect and maintain them. However, it does not apply to **all private assets**, but to resources like **water bodies, forests, and other natural assets**.
 
• In the context of the case, the application of this doctrine to all private assets would have been deemed **overarching and unjustified**.
 
 
 
• **State can acquire all private properties at will**__
 __
 
• This option is incorrect because it contradicts the Indian Constitution's principles, particularly **Article 300A**, which ensures that private property can only be acquired by the state under legal authority.
 
• Such unrestricted acquisition would lead to potential misuse of power and infringe upon **individual rights**.
 
 
 
• **Government power overrides individual property rights**__
 
 
• This option undermines the balance between government authority and private rights as established in the Constitution of India.
 
• While the government has the right to acquire property for public purposes, it must adhere to **legal procedures** and ensure fair compensation.

__
 
• **Overseas Citizen of India (OCI)** is a special status provided to **foreign nationals of Indian origin** by the Government of India under Section 7A of the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
• OCI status does not grant **dual citizenship**. Instead, it provides foreign nationals with **special privileges** such as visa-free travel to India and certain rights to participate in economic and educational activities.
 
• OCI cardholders are allowed to live and work in India indefinitely without the need for a visa.
 
• However, they do not have **voting rights**, cannot hold **constitutional posts**, or contest elections in India.
 
• OCI cardholders can own property in India except for agricultural land, plantation property, or a farmhouse.
 
• This status is primarily aimed at the **Indian diaspora** to help them stay connected to their roots while residing abroad.
 
• The scheme was introduced in **2005** and later merged with the Person of Indian Origin (PIO) card scheme in **2015**.

 __
 
• Only **Indian citizens** are eligible to hold constitutional posts such as the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister, or Chief Justice of India.
 
• OCI holders are foreign nationals and are thus not entitled to hold such posts.
 
 
 
• **Indian citizens with voting rights**__
 __
 
• OCI cardholders are not **Indian citizens**, hence they do not have voting rights. Only individuals with Indian citizenship are eligible to vote in elections.
 
 
 
• **Dual citizens of India and another country**__
 
 
• India does not allow **dual citizenship**. It only provides the OCI card as a recognition of a person’s Indian origin and to grant certain privileges.

Expression: 4 × ((6/4)x² − 25x + 12) − 6 × (x² + 5x − 13)

**Concept Used:**

Use the distributive property of multiplication over addition and subtraction: a(b ± c) = ab ± ac

**Calculation:**

⇒ (4 × (6/4)x²) − (4 × 25x) + (4 × 12) − (6 × x²) − (6 × 5x) − (6 × −13)

⇒ 6x² − 100x + 48 − 6x² − 30x + 78

Grouping the like terms together (the x² terms, x terms, and constant terms):

⇒ (6x² − 6x²) + (−100x − 30x) + (48 + 78)

⇒ 0 − 130x + 126

⇒ −130x + 126

**∴ The correct answer is −130x + 126.**

BODMAS Rule

It defines the correct sequence to solve mathematical expressions: Brackets, Order, Division, Multiplication, Addition, and Subtraction.

Distributive Property

The distributive property states that multiplying a sum by a number is the same as multiplying each addend by the number and then adding the products: a(b + c) = ab + ac.

Like Terms

Terms whose variables and their exponents are exactly the same are called like terms. Only like terms can be added or subtracted from each other to simplify algebraic expressions.

⇒ Sum of digits = 3 + 8 + 6 + 9 + 3 + 7 + 3 + 5 + 5 = 49.

⇒ Since 49 is not divisible by 3, the given number is not divisible by 3.

⇒ Option 2 (Divisibility by 15): A number must be divisible by both 3 and 5 to be divisible by 15.

⇒ Since the number fails the divisibility test for 3, it is not divisible by 15.

⇒ Option 4 (Divisibility by 14): A number must be even to be divisible by an even number like 14.

⇒ Option 3 (Divisibility by 5): A number is divisible by 5 if its last digit is either 0 or 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5.**

Divisibility Rule of 3 & 9

A number is divisible by 3 or 9 if the sum of all its digits is divisible by 3 or 9 respectively.

Divisibility Rule of 4 & 8

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits form a number divisible by 4. It is divisible by 8 if its last three digits form a number divisible by 8.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule of Composite Numbers

To check divisibility by a composite number (like 12 or 15), check divisibility by its co-prime factors (e.g., 3 and 4 for 12; 3 and 5 for 15).

To find the smallest number to be added, use: Number to be added = Divisor − Remainder.

Divide the given number 16809 by 41.

⇒ 409 = 41 × 9 + 40

⇒ Therefore, 16809 = 41 × 409 + 40

⇒ The remainder obtained is 40.

⇒ The required number to reach the next complete multiple = Divisor − Remainder.
